The same formica table, the same lamp. Marek VRABEC has kept his railwayman's jacket on. His hands are black with grease; he holds them flat on the table, as he was told.

"They brought me up from Brenec last night. Three hours on the train for the signalman who supposedly delays the trains."
« La signalisation gèle, l'hiver, au km: "The signals freeze in winter, at km 47. They jam, you have to get down and clear the points by hand. I write down what I see. What else should I write?"
« Qui monte dans le 2241 à Brenec, la nu: "Who boards the 2241 at Brenec, at night?"
Il hésite. « Qui voulez-vous qui monte à: He hesitates. "Who do you think boards at Brenec at night? Village people. Those who work on the other side, those with family in Halvek. Taking the train isn't a crime."
Les mains se crispent. « Pavel est parti: His hands clench. "Pavel left in '81. By that line, yes, the one I keep. You wanted to hear it? There, it's said. I know the ones who stay on this side, and what it is to wait for someone on the other."
« Vous savez ce que le décret prévoit, p: "Do you know what the decree provides for, at the border?"
VRABEC relève la tête. « Je sais lire le: VRABEC raises his head. "I can read the bulletins, inspector. The decree, the severity, the foreign agents." He spreads his hands. "Do your job. I did mine for thirty years: keeping the line open." You get nothing more.
Il regarde ses mains noires. « Mon fils: He looks at his black hands. "My son went that way, in '81. I couldn't follow him any more, so I kept the door open for the others. Five nights. I held the train back long enough for them to cross the tracks." A silence. "Write what you like. I kept the time, not the border."
Il lit le relevé du régulateur longtemps:
He reads the dispatcher's log for a long time. Then he puts the sheet down, very gently.

"... All right. The signals didn't fail. I held the 2241 for twelve minutes, on the good nights. Long enough for them to get off, hug their people on the Halvek platform, get back on. Twelve minutes. Write it down."
« Vous avez les noms. Irena, Stefan... d: "You have the names. Irena, Stefan... neighbours." He shrugs. "And what are you looking for at the end of the list? My bank account? I never took a penny. Not a coin, not an egg. Ask in Brenec."
Il lit le mot « filière » et quelque cho:
He reads the word "network" and something breaks in his face — not fear, tiredness.

"A network." He laughs without a sound. "They're mothers and sons, inspector, not spies. There's no leader, no money, no foreigner. There's a border in the middle of a village, and a train that passes once a night. That's all there is."
« Un groupe non identifié. » Il secoue l: "An unidentified group." He shakes his head. "The 23rd, yes. The permits had just been cancelled, on the 20th. So they boarded anyway, because on the other side an old woman won't last the winter. Your unidentified group was four people who already knew they wouldn't come back."
VRABEC regarde le papier, puis vous. « J: VRABEC looks at the paper, then at you. "I don't see what you want me to say about it, inspector."
Le planton raccompagne VRABEC. Sur le se: The orderly shows VRABEC out. On the threshold, he turns around: "The 2241 leaves at 22h40. If it leaves on time tonight, it means nobody was waiting." He does not wish you all the best.
